note: This file only claims milestones backed by physical repository records. CORE_CONTENT_COMPLETE means the evidence-backed core path is coherent and physically represented; it does not assert exhaustive coverage of every vendor feature, organization-specific procedure, or workload edge case.

paths.title: Active Directory Specialist / Senior Wintel Engineer
paths.target_role: AD Specialist / Senior Wintel Engineer / Infrastructure Engineer
entry_prerequisites: Working knowledge of Windows Server administration, TCP/IP and enterprise change control

milestones.rationale: Start with replication because AD consistency, DNS-integrated data, Group Policy and recovery all depend on understanding convergence and failure age.
Add DNS/DC Locator and site/subnet topology so authentication and replication symptoms can be traced through their network dependencies.
Build operations-master and time-hierarchy competence before advanced lifecycle or recovery decisions.
Combine Kerberos and secure-channel evidence so learners can separate identity, time, DNS and machine-trust failures.
Cover Group Policy architecture, LDAP protections and delegated OU administration as the main policy and least-privilege control plane.
Develop service-account hygiene and automation-aware identity administration with gMSA.
Cover branch RODC design, functional levels, Global Catalog considerations and domain-controller lifecycle/metadata-cleanup boundaries.
Finish technical progression with trusted backups, object/domain recovery semantics and forest-recovery readiness.
Conclude with cross-domain assessment, senior interview judgement and an enterprise health/recovery capstone rather than isolated factual recall.

paths.dependency_notes: M1-M4 establish core directory, discovery, FSMO/time and authentication reasoning. M5-M7 add policy, security and lifecycle design. M8 is intentionally late because recovery is high-impact and assumes the learner can reason about replication, DNS, FSMO and authentication dependencies. M9 is the integrated evidence gate.
paths.status_rationale: The path has physical coverage across replication, DNS/DC Locator, sites/subnets, FSMO, time hierarchy, Kerberos, secure channels, Group Policy, LDAP security, OU delegation, gMSA, RODC, functional levels/Global Catalog, DC lifecycle, backup/restore and forest recovery, with integrated assessments, interviews and capstone evidence. Organization-specific procedures and the long tail of AD DS features remain future enrichment.

paths.title: Windows Server / Wintel Specialist
paths.target_role: Windows Server Engineer / Senior Wintel Engineer / Infrastructure Engineer
entry_prerequisites: Basic TCP/IP, virtualization and enterprise change-control awareness

milestones.rationale: Establish supported Windows Server installation, role, lifecycle and evidence-collection fundamentals before deeper operations.
Build servicing, WSUS/update, event, service and remote-management operational discipline.
Develop storage/filesystem, networking and time-series performance troubleshooting competence.
Add SMB/file-service security, Storage Spaces, Windows Server 2025 role-aware hardening and crash-evidence preservation.
Finish technical progression with VSS-aware backup/recovery engineering and failover-cluster evidence-based operations.
Conclude with cumulative assessment, senior incident judgement and a non-production operations/security/recovery capstone.

paths.dependency_notes: W1-W2 establish platform and servicing operations. W3 adds core storage/network/performance troubleshooting. W4 adds security and advanced operations. W5 adds recovery and clustering only after core operational reasoning is established. W6 is the integrated evidence gate.
paths.status_rationale: The evidence-backed Windows/Wintel core now spans installation/lifecycle, servicing, operational management, storage/filesystems, networking, performance, SMB/security hardening, crash diagnostics, backup/VSS/system recovery and failover-cluster operations, with five assessments, five senior interview modules and an integrated capstone. Product-specific application administration and the long tail of Windows roles remain future enrichment.
